title: Malta (Acts 28:1–16)
hook: islanders show unusual kindness, a fire in the rain, a viper shaken off
tomorrow: Paul finally reaches Rome, in chains. how does Acts end?

segments.voice: Yesterday, bread broken on a breaking ship, and everyone ashore. The line: all came safe to land.

Cold rain, wet clothes, and the smell of woodsmoke from somewhere up the beach. Acts 27 left a crowd of soaked strangers on an island called Melita: sailors, soldiers, prisoners. The islanders owe them nothing. So who lights the fire? They do: "the barbarous people shewed us no little kindness: for they kindled a fire, and received us every one, because of the present rain, and because of the cold." The King James calls them barbarous, and in the same breath, they're the kind ones.
screen: `RAIN, COLD, WOODSMOKE.` → `THE ISLANDERS LIGHT THE FIRE.` → `RECEIVED US EVERY ONE.`

segments.voice: Paul pitches in, gathering a bundle of sticks for the fire, and "there came a viper out of the heat, and fastened on his hand." The islanders reach a verdict fast: this man must be a murderer; the sea let him go, but justice won't. Paul "shook off the beast into the fire, and felt no harm." They wait for him to swell up or drop dead. Nothing. So they change their minds and call him a god. Two verdicts, murderer then god, and Acts doesn't argue with either. It keeps telling what people do. Publius, the chief man of the island, lodges them three days. Paul prays for his father, sick with a fever, and he's healed, and others come. When the ship leaves, the islanders load it with what they need. Back in Athens, Paul told the philosophers that God "hath made of one blood all nations of men." On this island, people who never heard that sentence lived it first: a fire in the rain, and every stranger let in.
screen: `A VIPER SHAKEN OFF.` · `MURDERER, THEN A GOD.` · `PUBLIUS, AND A FEVER HEALED.` · `OF ONE BLOOD, LIVED FIRST.` · then, large: `NO LITTLE KINDNESS.`

segments.voice: Rub your palms together until they're warm, then rest them open on your knees. Listen for one sound around you, rain, a fan, traffic, and stay with it and with the warmth in your hands, the way a fire feels to someone just pulled out of the sea.
Malta. The island Acts calls Melita, where strangers lit a fire in the rain and took in every one.
Pocket this one: no little kindness, given before anyone knew a thing about anyone. Until tomorrow.

screen: `DAY 1530 COUNTS.` → `ACTS, READ THROUGH · 44 OF 45.` → `TOMORROW: PAUL FINALLY REACHES ROME, IN CHAINS. HOW DOES ACTS END?`

howItsDone: Some churches read Acts 28 when they speak of welcoming strangers, and Christians in Malta remember Paul's shipwreck as part of their island's story.

fork.setup: a new kid sits alone at lunch. your friends have already decided he's 'weird.' what would Malta's islanders do?
options: wait to see if he's actually weird before saying hi.
make room at the table before you know a thing.
invite him only if someone you trust vouches for him.
fork.reveal: the islanders kindled a fire and received every one, before they knew who was a prisoner and who was a soldier.

original.note: Greek: kindness to people. In Acts 28:2 the King James gives it as no little kindness.

trapdoor: what you thought: a snakebite miracle.
what it means: strangers who owed nothing lit a fire, took everyone in, and kept giving until the ship sailed.
what a scholar hears: φιλανθρωπίαν in 28:2, kindness to people, and 'barbarous' as the King James word for the islanders.

chat.says: the neighbor we always complain about (loud truck) mowed our lawn and left soup. for dad. i feel weird.
options: Maybe you misjudged him a little. Thank him in person, and take the bowl back clean.
He probably wants something. Be polite, but keep your distance until you know why.
Just text a thanks. Neighbors do that stuff; it doesn't need to change anything.
chat.meaning: The islanders owed the castaways nothing and lit a fire anyway, and their own snap verdict on Paul changed. Kindness from someone you'd written off is worth receiving and answering.

Melita.meaning: the name Acts gives the island, taken to be Malta
